title: Polygon triangulations and flips
notes: Keep one adult at each of the three tables; adults can trace or record a child-chosen filling. On a return visit, K-1 can keep a line while completing a polygon (P4) or change one line (P5-6). Grades 2-3 can use their pentagon gallery for the flip map and odd return (P4-5), with the hexagon one-flip and shortest-route problems (P3, P6), leaving the full hexagon collection (P7) for a separate investigation. Grades 4-5 can revisit shortest fan routes (P4-5) and then the general fan rule or connectivity (P6-7). Preserve labeled tracings between visits.

Provide eleven pencils/straightedges for the current 4/4/3 children and about 28 tracing sheets cut into quarters, about ten quarters per child (page 2). Existing polygon sizes and straightedge conventions are unchanged.
